cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul, the apostle writing to the church in Corinth, says, "In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool." He tags his own words as fool talk before anybody else can, friends. Most folks brag first and add the disclaimer never.

The answer is that many are already boasting. Paul says, "Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast." He just called it fool talk, and I think he'd rather not. It's like a coworker bragging all week until you finally have to speak up.

The answer is True. Paul says the Corinthians put up with "…anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face." That's a heavy list, so let's just let it sit. I think Paul is pointing at how much they'll put up with, and he's about to turn that toward himself.

The word is match. Paul says, "Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about." He isn't saying he'll beat them yet, friends. He's just saying he can stand toe to toe with them. It's like walking into a bake sale with your own tray and saying, "Go ahead, set yours down."

The answer is Abraham. Paul says, "Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I." Abraham is the man God made promises to (Genesis 12:2 and 3). Paul has the family papers, and he isn't afraid to pull them out.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…I am so much more…" which is a lot further than equal. He backs it up with "harder labor," "more imprisonments," "worse beatings" and "…frequent danger of death." That's the kind of list you don't read quickly, friends.

The answer is three times. Paul says, "…three times I was shipwrecked." Three! I'd have taken one look at a boat after the first one and started walking everywhere. And Paul is telling the Corinthians all of this himself.

The answer is True. Paul lists "…danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles…" which means danger from his own people and from the non-Jews. He also lists danger "…in the city and in the country…" and "…on the sea and among false brothers…" Danger just kept switching addresses on him.

The answer is sleep and food. Paul says he was "…often without sleep…" and "…often without food…" He adds hunger and thirst, cold and exposure too. A rough list, friends. Even my cookie timer gets more rest than that.

The answer is concern for all the churches. Paul says, "Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches." He means the people, not just the places. Every day he carries all of them. I think that's a heavy load, friends.

The word is weakness. Paul says, "If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness." After a whole list of beatings and shipwrecks, he picks weakness. That's a boast you don't hear at the cookie swap, friends. Most folks lead with their best batch.

The answer is True. Paul says, "The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying." He calls on God Himself as the one who knows. When you've just listed all that, you might want somebody to turn to who knows the whole story. And God is the one Paul names.

The answer is that he was lowered in a basket through a window. Paul says, "…I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp." After all those beatings and shipwrecks, he picks this for his boast. A basket! I've been carried in a drawer, but never lowered out of a window.
